(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice K Natarajan) Criminal Petition No.201120/2024 filed by the
petitioner/accused No.1 and Criminal Petition No.200512/2024 filed by the petitioners/accused
Nos.2 to 6 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.9007/2023
arising out of Crime No.111/2023 registered by Kalaburagi City Women Police Station and
charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under Section 498-A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34
of Ipc and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the
D.P.Act').
2.

During pendency of the petitions, the accused No.1 in Criminal Petition No.201120/2024 and respondent No.2 appeared and filed joint compromise application in I.A.No.1/2024 under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking permission of this Court for compounding the offence.
The learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 are present.

4. Both petitioner/accused No.1 and respondent No.2 present and submit both of them joined together and leading happy marital life and they stayed separately from the parents of the petitioner/accused No.1.
5.

In view of the undertaking given by the petitioner/accused No.1 and the respondent No.2 joining together, leading happy marital life and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another reported in (2012) SCC 303, the Court can permit the parties to compound the offence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Accordingly, I.A.No.1/2024 filed by the petitioner/accused No.1 and respondent No.2 is hereby allowed.
7. The Criminal Petition No.200512/2024 filed by petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 6 i.e. in-laws of respondent NC: 2024:KHC-K:6861 No.2.
In view of the compromise entered into between the accused No.1 and respondent No.2/complainant, both are joining together and leading marital life,
hence, criminal proceedings against accused No.1 required to be quashed.
Therefore, continuing the criminal proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 6 is nothing but abuse of process of law and liable to be quashed.
Therefore, both the petitions are deserve to be allowed.

8. Accordingly, I pass the following:
